Agentic AI

Where the agent works over a whole list rather than one part at a time, its tile also shows what is waiting for attention right now, and a Fix with AI link that opens the screen and runs the agent immediately — it still only proposes: nothing is saved, assigned or closed without a person reviewing it on Review Agent Work.

Roles & Responsibilities

Sheets on file

Succession Planning

Who could do the job if the person doing it stopped tomorrow. Readiness is not an opinion typed in here: each candidate is measured against the competency map for the target role, using the levels on the skill matrix. Ready now means no gap; ready with training means a gap of one level and nothing on safety or quality; not ready means anything more than that.

Where the works is exposed

Posts held by one person with nobody ready to take over. Worked out from the sanctioned strength, who is on the roll, and the readiness above — it is not a list somebody maintains.

Competency Mapping

What level a designation has to reach on each machine or operation. This is the only screen in the chain where a requirement is decided; everything after it — the gap, the training need, whether the training worked — is worked out by comparing this against the skill matrix. Set it once per role, not per person, or the standard moves every time somebody leaves.

Requirements

Skill Gap Analysis

Nothing on this screen is typed. Each person's designation gives the level their role requires; the skill matrix gives the level they have been assessed at. Where the second is short of the first, that is a gap — and a gap on a machine somebody is already booked on is the one to look at first.
Suggested training priority

Training Need Identification

Two kinds of need reach this screen. The ones found by the gap analysis arrive on their own and cannot be typed or deleted — they go when the skill is assessed, not when somebody ticks them. The ones that come from somewhere else — a new machine, a statutory refresher, a customer requirement, a non-conformance — are added below.

Needs found by the gap analysis

Needs recorded by hand

Training Plan vs Actual

One record per session, planned first and completed afterwards. A session cannot be marked done without a date and somebody who attended — a training record with no attendees is the one an auditor asks about. The plan-against-actual figure on the HR dashboard is counted from these records, so nothing has to be typed there.

Sessions

Session

Training Effectiveness

Whether the training changed anything on the shop floor. The level each attendee held on the day is read from the skill matrix history, and the level they hold now is read from the same place — so "improved" is something the records show, not something the trainer says. Effectiveness cannot be judged the same week: a session is only offered here once 30 days have passed, because the question is whether it stuck, not whether it was enjoyed.

Capacity Plan

Hours needed against hours available, machine by machine and month by month. The production plan answers whether there is enough capacity overall; this answers when it runs out, which is the question that decides whether you buy a machine or work a third shift. Demand comes from the open orders and the routing cycle times; nothing is estimated.

What to do about it

What each machine can do

Shifts, hours and working days are per machine, because they are not the same for every machine in a real works. Availability is what is left after planned maintenance, setting and the rest — set it from the actual figure on the production dashboard rather than from 100%, or this plan will promise hours that do not exist. Changes save as you make them.

Machine Loading Plan

The open orders put onto the machines in date order, one after another, until each machine's day is full — so an order that cannot be started until the machine ahead of it is clear shows the date it will actually finish, not the date somebody hoped for. Two assumptions worth knowing: an operation finishes before the next one on the same order starts (no overlapping batches), and earliest due date is loaded first. It is a projection from today's order book, not a commitment.

What to do about it

Bill of Materials

What one piece of this part consumes. Materials come from the material master, not free text, so what is consumed here and what was received on a goods receipt are the same thing and can be netted off. Rates are read from the master every time this is opened — they are not copied in, so a rate revision does not leave old bills quoting a price nobody charges any more.

Lines

Raw Material Stock

Nothing on this screen is typed except the opening balance. Stock is opening + accepted receipts − what production consumed, worked out from the goods receipts, the inward inspections and the production bookings against each part's bill of materials. Material that has been received but not yet inspected is shown separately and is not counted as stock, because it is not yours to use until it passes.

SPC — Control Charts

Statistical process control, per the SPC Manual, drawn from the readings the operators already record on the self-inspection sheets — nothing is entered twice. Each check records one piece, so the chart is an individuals and moving range chart; an X̄–R chart would need several pieces per check and drawing one from single readings would put limits on the page that mean nothing. Beyond the control limits, the chart also checks the Western Electric zone tests (Zone A and Zone B), a run on one side of the average, and a steady trend — and works out Cp/Cpk (potential capability) and Pp/Ppk (performance capability) against the drawing tolerance once there are enough readings.

Setup Wizard

Six steps, in order — each one saves as you go, so there is nothing separate to remember to save at the end. Skip ahead any time using the dots, or use Sample Data on Step 5 to explore with example records before typing in your own.

1 · Company profile

These details appear on every quotation, invoice and printed document.

More fields — bank details, signature, logo — are on Company Profile directly, any time.

2 · Who else needs a login

You are signed in as —. Add the people who will use this system day to day — an estimator does not need the same access as an administrator.

Fine-grained access per person is on User Management.

3 · The masters everything else is built on

A routing needs a part and a machine to exist first; an order needs a customer. Add a few of each now, by hand or from a spreadsheet — the rest of the system has nothing to work with until these do.

Have these in a spreadsheet already? Bulk Upload does all four in one go.

4 · Statutory rates and HR rules

PF, ESI, professional tax and TDS come from your CA, not a guess — this step only checks whether they have been entered yet, and takes you straight there.

5 · Try it, or start entering real data

Not ready to type in real records yet? Load example data across every screen, click around risk-free, then clear it before going live. This is the same Sample Data feature as Admin → Sample Data.

6 · Connections

Email, AI and WhatsApp. Each one says whether it is actually working, how to get what it needs, and lets you test it for real before you rely on it.

Email checking…
Sends you an alert when an RFQ arrives, and sends quotations to customers.
How to get a Resend API key
  1. Go to resend.com and sign up — free at this volume.
  2. Left menu → API Keys → Create API Key. Any name will do.
  3. Copy the key straight away — it starts re_ and is shown only once.
  4. Paste it below and press Save email.

To send from your own domain: Resend → Domains → Add Domain, add the DNS records it gives you exactly as shown, then press Verify. Until that says Verified, use onboarding@resend.dev — but it only delivers to the address you registered with Resend, so customers will receive nothing.

AI checking…
Reads drawings, plans process routes, drafts documents and powers every agent. Optional — everything else works without it. One provider is enough; the others are fallbacks.
WhatsApp checking…
Optional, alongside email. Needs a Meta WhatsApp Business account and an approved message template.
Keep your own copy of these keys
Only the administrator login can read these keys back. Everyone else can set them and test them here, which is what this screen is for.
Backup & Restore exports these masked on purpose — a backup file travels between deployments and inboxes, and one carrying a working key is a leak waiting to happen. This is the one place they can be read back, so a flush, a re-deployment or a new database does not mean reissuing every key at every provider. Keys set as Vercel environment variables are not included: they are not this system's to hand out, and a flush cannot lose them.
The file this downloads holds your keys in the clear. Anyone who opens it can send email as your company, spend your AI credit and message your customers. Keep it where you keep passwords — not in a shared drive, not attached to an email. Every download is recorded in the audit trail with who did it and when.
Records, parts, orders and documents are a separate backup — Admin → Backup & Restore, the Data & records half.

7 · Done

That is everything this wizard checks. Nothing is locked — come back to any step at any time from Admin → Setup Wizard, or jump straight to any screen from the menu.

Parts, BOM & routing

This panel used to hold a second, simplified part list with its own bill of materials and routing, typed in here by hand. It has been removed, because every part has its own BOM and its own routing and neither of them belongs on a settings screen:
  • When quoting — RFQ Pipeline reads the customer's drawing and works out the route, the cycle times and the bill of materials for that part from what the drawing actually says. Every line is editable on the costing sheet.
  • Once it is won — that route is written onto the real part with Send route to the part, where Process Master, Bill of Materials and the Dimensions Master own it from then on, and the PFD, PFMEA and control plan are all built from it.
What stays on this screen is what a quotation genuinely needs and a part cannot supply: the machines and their rates, the labour grades, the material price book and the cost base above.

Backup & Restore

Two separate halves, kept apart on purpose. Settings & admin is what makes this deployment look like your company — profile, branding, website content, rates, provider keys. Data & records is the work itself — parts, orders, routings, production, quality, HR. Each half has its own download, its own upload and its own flush, so you can replace one without disturbing the other. Restoring overwrites any record with the same id and cannot be undone.

Settings & admin data

Company profile and branding, website content and theme, login screen, quoting and costing rates, statutory rates, document numbering, registered devices and provider keys. Does not contain a single part, order or employee.
Wipes everything listed above for a fresh deploy. Does not touch user accounts — remove those from User Management — and does not touch any data. Download first if there is any chance you will want it back; this cannot be undone.

Data & records

Everything every other screen has saved — parts, customers, suppliers, machines, routings, quality documents, production, dispatch, HR records and enquiries. Does not contain your company profile, branding or any key.
Deletes every part, order, routing, quality document, production booking, attendance record, punch, payslip and attachment. Does not touch your company profile, branding, users, keys or devices — the same team carries straight on afterwards. That now includes the pictures: the logo, the hero banner and video and every image on the website are kept, because the website content still points at them. Only files attached to the records being deleted go. Download first; this cannot be undone.

KPI & Appraisal

A KPI is either typed in by hand or read live from records already on file — never both, and a card always says which. Appraisals pull the competency position straight from the Skill Matrix and Competency Mapping, so the numbers here can never disagree with those screens. Three auto sources are wired up natively — attrition, competency and open tasks. On-time delivery, absenteeism and training closure still read from data that has not moved off the website yet, so those sources stay on HR & Payroll's engine for now rather than compute something this screen cannot stand behind.

Audit Readiness

Nothing to fill in — each check reads records that already exist elsewhere and says, plainly, whether an auditor asking for that evidence today would find it. Green means the evidence exists; amber means it exists but is incomplete; red means it does not exist yet. Training-session effectiveness is not checked here yet — training sessions have not moved off the website's HR engine, and a check against the wrong record would be worse than no check at all.

Payroll

A pay run is built as a draft from the attendance already marked for the period, checked line by line, then approved. Every rate comes from Statutory & Masters — nothing here carries a hard-coded figure. An approved pay run cannot be edited, reopened or deleted; a correction is a new run, because an approved run is a financial record.

Build a draft pay run

Payable days come from the attendance register for that month. Anyone with no attendance marked is included at zero payable days and flagged, rather than quietly left out of their own payslip.

Nothing is entered here. It reads the routings already built on Process Master Configuration and cross-references them against the Machine Addition master — by machine, so you can see everything that runs on it before routing a new part to it, or by process, so you can see every machine that has already run a given operation.

Every operation

On the Machine Addition master, active, but not named on any operation — idle, not yet routed to, or worth checking is still needed.

Non-conformance and corrective action

Everything else in this system finds problems. This is where one gets closed out. Raise it against the record it came from, so the rejection and the action are the same thread — an auditor asks to see both.

Open actions

What is still owed, and to whom. An action with no owner and no date is a wish, so both are shown and the overdue ones come first.
Who to chase first

Works Dashboard

What the works looks like right now, read across every module. Each number is a link to the screen it came from — nothing here is a figure you cannot go and check.

Needs somebody today

Production

Customer PO

New parts

Customer PO

Two kinds of PO, because customers send both. A one-time PO is complete in itself — quantity, price and a delivery date, valid for a stated period. A rate contract PO only fixes the part and the price; the customer sends the actual quantities later as schedules against it, and a schedule always takes its part number, part name and price from the contract it is raised against — never typed twice, so a schedule can never end up priced differently from the contract that set the rate.
Quantities the customer has indicated but not yet ordered. They become demand in the Sales Plan for those two months, and are replaced by a real PO for that month the moment one exists — never added on top of it.

Customer PO register — live

Sales Plan

The plan is arrived at, not typed: every Customer PO due in a month, and every schedule released against a rate contract and due in that month, is demand — added up here automatically by customer and part. Tentative quantities entered on a Customer PO for the two months after it count as demand for those months too, until a real PO replaces them.

Sales Plan register

Demand quantity is the total of every Customer PO and schedule due to that customer, for that part, in this month — including any tentative quantity carried forward from an earlier PO. Actual quantity is the total invoiced, taken from Sales Invoice. Nothing here is typed twice.

Previous month —

The month before the one above, for comparison: what was carried, what was billed, and what was left behind.

Jig & Fixture Master

A jig or fixture belongs to one part and one operation, so that is what makes it the same item: the same description on the same part and operation is refused as a duplicate. The code is issued by the database. Items that came across from an RFQ costing are marked Provisional until somebody confirms them here.

Jigs & fixtures

RM Purchase Orders

Raw material ordered but not yet received. The Planning Module counts the open quantity as on order, so material already on its way is not ordered twice. Received quantity is worked out from the goods receipts of that material dated on or after the PO date, oldest PO first — nothing is typed twice. A PO that will never be completed is short-closed, which stops its balance being counted.
Lines

Purchase orders

Planning Module

One click, once the Sales Plan has arrived. Each PO and schedule line is netted in delivery-date order: gross requirement − despatched − usable part stock (+ FG safety stock) = net requirement, grossed up for the process rejection allowance and rounded up to the batch size = balance to start at the 1st operation, due to start manufacturing lead time before delivery. That is exploded through the BOM into raw material and netted against RM on hand (accepted) and RM already on order, plus RM safety stock, rounded up to the MOQ = RM to purchase, to be ordered supplier lead time before the start date. Every piece and every kilo is counted once.

Material requirement plan

Nothing worked out yetPress Run Planning.

Raw material to purchase

The list MMD raises purchase orders from: required + safety stock − on hand (accepted) − on order, rounded up to the MOQ / pack size. Material awaiting inward inspection is shown but not counted until it passes. Order-by is the earliest start date that needs it, less the supplier lead time.

Part stock position

Each piece is counted once, in the stage it is in now: WIP = OK at each in-house operation − taken into the next (job-work operations: sent on returnable challan / accepted back) · FI = OK at the last operation − offered to PDI · FG = PDI accepted − despatched · Supplier = sent on returnable job-work challans − received back on GRN · Incoming = part GRNs not yet inspected. Rejected, on-hold and rework quantities are shown for information and are never counted as usable. Type a physical count to replace a figure until you clear it.

Sales Invoice

Raising this creates a real tax invoice — one customer, one invoice number, one or more parts on it — and prints it. Every line becomes dispatched quantity the moment it is saved: Sales Plan and the dashboards read straight from these lines, so nothing is entered twice. Each line is raised against a Customer PO, chosen from the POs on file for that customer and part; the PO number and date on the invoice come from there, never retyped. A line that takes a customer/part past that month's demand is flagged as excess, not silently absorbed into the total.
Ship to — filled from the customer; change it when the goods go somewhere else
Charges — discount and charges go into the taxable value, as GST requires
E-invoice — only if applicable: copy these from the e-invoice portal once the IRN is generated

Lines on this invoice

Manufacturing / traceability — optional, printed on the invoice for this line
Invoice settings — UPI, terms, jurisdiction and copies, set once for every invoice
Company name, address, GSTIN, PAN, phone, email, website and bank account come from the Company Profile. What only the invoice needs is kept here.

Invoice register

Sales Plan vs Actual — overall

Quantity, then value in INR and USD kept apart — value comes from the customer/part price link and the invoice rate, never converted between the two.

Customer vs Sales Plan vs Actual

Quantity columns first, then plan / actual / pending value for each currency the customer buys in.

Overall Sales Value — day wise

What was actually invoiced each day this month, in INR — from Sales Invoice, the same figures the plan vs actual above is measured against.

Sales Value by Customer — day wise

The same day-by-day figures, split out per customer — which days a customer's business clusters on, not just the total.

Excess sales — invoiced over the plan

Quantity invoiced to a customer for a part, in a month, beyond what that month's firm plan allowed — including invoices raised against a customer/part with no plan line at all for that month.

Production Plan

What is still to make against each order, and the rate needed to hit the date. Made and despatched come from the production bookings and the cleared lots, not from anybody's estimate. Whether the machines actually have the hours is answered on Capacity Plan and Machine Loading Plan — one calculation, not repeated here.

Capacity check

Machine-by-machine hours against demand, month by month, is worked out on Capacity Plan. Where each order actually lands in the machine queue, with a real projected finish date, is worked out on Machine Loading Plan. Both read the same open orders and routings as this screen.

Production Entry

What was actually made, on which machine, by whom, and what went wrong. A job cannot be booked against an operation with no approved setup — that is what the setup approval is for.

Review agent work

Everything an agent has proposed and nobody has yet accepted. Approving is not a formality. An operation or a characteristic the AI proposed is a guess until an engineer has checked it against the drawing — putting your name to it says you have. Rejecting removes it, with the reason kept.

Pending

Supplier Watch Agent

Works out how each supplier is actually performing from the goods receipts and inward inspections already on file — rejection rate, deviations accepted, repeat problems, receipts left uninspected. The figures are arithmetic; the AI is asked only which conversations to have first. It changes nothing and it does not rate anyone by opinion.

Suppliers

What needs attention

NPD Agent

Takes a part from where it is to a full draft set — routing, dimensions, flow, PFMEA, control plan — one step at a time. It stops at anything it cannot do honestly and tells you why. Everything it writes is a draft. It signs nothing and approves nothing; the AI's proposals are marked as such wherever they appear, so nobody mistakes them for engineering that has been done.

Plan

Audit Readiness Agent

Reads across every module and reports what an auditor would find. The checks themselves are arithmetic, not opinion — the agent runs them, then asks the AI only to put them in the order a person should work through. It changes nothing. Every finding links to the screen where it can be fixed.

Findings

Agent Run Log

Every agent run is recorded: what it looked at, what it found, who started it. An agent that cannot be audited has no place in a quality system.

Pre-Despatch Inspection

The last check before parts leave. A lot that passes here is what releases a delivery challan — a challan cannot be raised against a part with no cleared lot unless somebody signs for despatching it anyway.

Readings

Lots

Measurement System Analysis — gauge R&R

The average-and-range study from the AIAG MSA manual. Take the same parts, measure them repeatedly with the same gauge by more than one operator, and the study says how much of what you are seeing is the part and how much is the measurement. A gauge that cannot tell your parts apart makes every inspection record taken with it worth less than it looks.

Readings

Studies

Gauge register and calibration

Every gauge named on a control plan needs a calibration status. The check below compares the register against the gauges your control plans actually call for — a gauge in use and not on the register is the first thing an auditor finds.
Which gauge to send for calibration first

Inward Inspection

Material that has been received but not yet inspected is listed below. Nothing here is typed twice — supplier, invoice, material and quantity come from the goods receipt. Until a receipt is inspected it should not be issued to production.

Inspection

Characteristics checked
Add one line per thing checked. A material certificate on its own is a line too.
Decision

Inspected

Self Inspection — in process

One sheet per operation per shift. The characteristics and the check frequency come from the control plan. Add a check each time the operator measures; anything out of tolerance has to be answered before the sheet can be closed, including what happened to the parts made since the last good check.

Sheet

Close the sheet

Closing is the operator's statement that the shift ran to the control plan. A sheet with an unanswered rejection cannot be closed.

Setup Approval — first-off

The characteristics come from the control plan for this operation, so an operator cannot be checking something different from what was agreed. Measure the first pieces, enter the readings, and the sheet works out whether each is in tolerance. A setup with anything out cannot be approved.

First-off readings

Approval

Approval releases the job to run. Whoever signs is saying the first pieces meet the drawing.

Recent setups

PPAP submission

The eighteen elements, per AIAG. What this system already holds is ticked automatically and shows the document it found — the rest you record as on file, not applicable, or leave outstanding. The warrant cannot be signed while anything required at the chosen level is outstanding.

Elements

Part Submission Warrant

Signing the warrant is a declaration to your customer that the parts meet their requirements and were made at the production rate. It is a statement someone is answerable for.

CNC Programme

Read this before you use anything on this screen. A drafted programme is a starting point for a programmer, not a programme to run. It has not been simulated, the offsets and work coordinates are assumptions, and no machine here knows your fixtures. Post it to a control without proving it out and you will crash a spindle. Every file this screen produces carries that warning inside it, and it cannot be marked proven until someone puts their name to a dry run.

Programme

Prove-out record

Filled in after the programme has been run in single block with feed override down and the first part measured. Until then the programme stays marked unproven wherever it appears.

Control Plan

Built from the PFMEA, the routing and the dimensions, so every control answers a failure mode that was actually ranked. An auditor cross-checks the two documents against each other — generating the control plan from anything else is how they come apart.

Control plan header (AIAG)

These fields print in the header block of the form, as required by the AIAG Control Plan format. They are not generated — enter them once per part and they are kept with the document.

Control Plan

Supplier / plant approval

A control plan is what the shop floor is held to. Until it is approved the printed copy is stamped DRAFT.

Process FMEA

Drafted by AI from the routing and the dimensions already on the part — every line is tied to a real operation and a real characteristic. Severity, occurrence and detection are starting points for your CFT to argue with, not answers. Nothing here is approved until a named team signs it.

PFMEA header (AIAG)

These fields print in the header block of the form, as required by the AIAG FMEA-4 format. They are not generated — enter them once per part and they are kept with the document.

PFMEA

Cross-functional team sign-off

A PFMEA is a team judgement, not a document one person produces. Record who reviewed it — the printed copy shows this, and until it is filled the print is stamped DRAFT.

Process Flow Diagram

Drawn from the routing — it is not typed separately, so it can never disagree with the operations you entered. Standard flowcharting symbols are used throughout: a box is an operation, a diamond is an inspection, and an inverted triangle is storage — the legend prints with the diagram.

Flow

Processes against a part

The route the part takes through the works, in order. Operation numbers step in tens so an operation can be inserted later without renumbering everything after it. This routing is what the PFD, the PFMEA and the control plan are all built from — nothing downstream can be generated until it exists.

Pull operations from the Costing Sheet

Reads the route already priced on a won enquiry for this part and offers those operations here — Process #, Process Name, Machine, Setup time and Cycle time — so they don't have to be re-typed. Choose which rows to bring across; each lands as its own operation, marked AI proposed until someone checks it on Review Agent Work, the same as a route sent from the RFQ Pipeline. An operation number already on this part is skipped, never overwritten.

Routing

Use ▲ / ▼ to change the sequence — it swaps the operation numbers of the two rows.

Dimensions against an operation

Every characteristic produced or checked at an operation. A dimension marked significant or critical is carried into the PFMEA and the control plan with the tighter treatment those require.

HR & Payroll

Everything about people, attendance and pay, in one place. Attendance is marked automatically by the fingerprint or face-recognition devices registered under Attendance Devices, and every screen here reads and writes the same employee, attendance, leave and pay records.

HR & Payroll

P present (device) · P marked or corrected by hand · ½ half day · A absent · CL approved leave · W weekly off · H holiday · – no punch and no mark (payroll counts it as absent) · a red corner is late, an amber corner a missed punch, +h overtime waiting for approval. Press any day to see its punches and correct it.
Use it after adding a Biometric ID to someone, changing a shift, or changing the late / half-day rules. Days marked by hand are left as they are.
Connect a biometric device — step by step
Follow the six steps below in order, once per device. Most fingerprint and face terminals sold in India work the same way — the device calls this site on its own (called "ADMS" or "push to server" on the device's menu); these steps cover that case. If your device only offers a Hikvision-style HTTP Listening setting, or a vendor's own middleware/webhook, do Steps 1, 2 and 3 the same way, then use the box under "Register a device" below instead of Step 4 — it shows the exact address for whichever connection type you choose there.
1
Check what you have
Two things, before you start
▼

1. The device's serial number. On most fingerprint and face terminals this is under Menu → System → System Info → Device Info (wording varies by make — look for "Serial Number" or "SN"). Write it down; you will need it in Step 3.

2. The device connected to your factory network, by network cable or Wi-Fi, with a working internet connection out of that network. The device does not need a fixed IP address or any port opened on your firewall for the common case in Step 4 — it calls out to this site itself, the same way a phone app does.

Why no firewall changes? The device is never reached from outside — it reaches out to this site's address on its own, the same direction a web browser works in. Nothing needs to be opened inward on your network for this.
2
Set your attendance rules
Plant time zone, shift and overtime — done once, in the section just below this guide
▼
Scroll down to Your attendance equipment and set your plant's time zone, which shift a punch counts against when none is named, how overtime from punches is treated, and how a single punch in a day should be read. Press Save there before going on. Late grace and the half-day cut-off come from the leave policy under Statutory & Masters, not from this screen — one set of rules, used by devices and payroll alike.
3
Register the device in the IDMS
In the "Register a device" section below this guide
▼

1. Give it a Name you will recognise later (e.g. "Main gate" or "Shop floor south").

2. Set Type to Fingerprint, Face recognition, or both, and Make to your device's brand — this only fills in the right connection type for you.

3. Leave How it sends punches on Push to server (ADMS / iclock) for a fingerprint or face terminal that calls out on its own — the common case.

4. Type in the Serial number from Step 1, and the device's Location.

5. Press Register device.

Didn't catch the serial number in Step 1? You can register the device first without one — point it at this site using Step 4 below, and it will appear in the Devices list further down as "Calling in — not registered" with its serial number already filled in from what it sent. Press Register next to it there instead.
4
Point the device at this site
On the device itself, using the exact address shown under the registration form
▼

On the device's own screen, go to Menu → Comm. (Communication) → Cloud Server Setting — some makes call this ADMS instead of "Cloud Server".

Turn Enable Domain Name (or "Domain Name Mode") ON, and fill in the Server Address and Server Port exactly as shown in the box under "Register a device" below, once you have chosen this device's connection type there — it is this site's own address, so it is always right whichever domain your IDMS runs on. Turn HTTPS on if the device offers the option.

Save the settings on the device. It will now call this site by itself, on its own schedule — there is nothing further to press here.

An older device that only offers plain HTTP, not HTTPS? It cannot reach a secure site directly. Export its log to a USB stick instead and use Import Device Log on the Employee Bulk Upload screen — the punches are read the same way either way once they arrive.
5
Test it
One punch, and a look at the Punch log below
▼
Scan a fingerprint or face on the device. Wait about a minute — the device reports in on a short delay, not instantly — then scroll down to Punch log, set From and To to today, and press Show punches. Your test scan should appear there, against the device's own internal user number for whoever scanned. If nothing appears after a few minutes, open the Devices list below and check the device's status — it should say "Reporting" if it has called in at all.
6
Match punches to people
One field on each employee record — done once per person, not per punch
▼
A punch is matched to a person by the Biometric ID field on their employee record, under HRM → People. Set it to the same user number the device itself gave that person when their fingerprint or face was enrolled (this is what showed up next to your test punch in Step 5). If it is left blank, their Employee ID is tried instead — so a device enrolled with the same numbers as your Employee IDs needs nothing set here at all. A punch that matches nobody is not lost: it is listed under Punch log → unmatched below, so you can see exactly which device user numbers still need a person attached.
Once everyone is matched, use Mark this month again from punches on the Attendance Register for anyone whose earlier scans were sitting unmatched — it works out their attendance from the punches now that they can be identified, without touching any day already marked by hand.
Your attendance equipment
Late grace and the half-day limit come from the leave policy, and shift times from the shift master, both under Statutory & Masters — one set of rules for devices and payroll alike.

Universal CNC Live Monitor

The IDMS reads one normalized machine data format, so the dashboard can work with FANUC, Siemens, Haas, Mazak, Mitsubishi, Okuma, Heidenhain and other controllers through the appropriate factory-LAN gateway/protocol adapter.
Waiting for machine data…

How machine connectivity works

CNC machines stay on the factory LAN. A small gateway reads the controller using MTConnect, vendor software such as FANUC FOCAS, OPC UA, Modbus TCP, or another supported adapter and sends only normalized telemetry to IDMS. This avoids locking the platform to one controller brand.
Used for production and tool-life counting.
Configured by part/operation in IDMS.
Calculated from machine events when available.
Remaining parts = life limit − parts used.

Attendance & Pay Lookup

Look up any employee's attendance, leave and pay position for the current or a past month. This reads the same records the employee's own self-service screen and payroll use — nothing here can be edited; go to People — HR records to change master data, or HR & Payroll to run payroll.

Company Legal Documents

The company's own statutory and legal papers — incorporation, GST, PAN, licences, certificates, insurance. Uploaded once, held in the backend, and available to view or download whenever an auditor, a customer or a bank asks for them. An expiry date is optional, but anything with one is flagged here before it runs out rather than after.

On file

Bulk Upload

Add many records at once from a spreadsheet instead of one at a time. Choose what you are adding. Each one opens its own upload: download the template so the columns are right, fill it in, upload it back, check the preview, then Import. Nothing is saved until Import — a bad row is reported, never silently skipped or saved wrong — and every imported record lands in the same database table as the screen named on its tile.

Bulk Upload

Connect your machines — step by step

Follow the seven steps below in order. You do not need to know any programming. Steps 1 to 3 take about ten minutes and are done once. Step 4 onwards is done on the PC that sits in the factory near your machines.
How this works, in one picture.
Your CNC machine → factory network cable → a small PC in the factory (the gateway) → internet → this IDMS.

The machine is never put on the internet. The gateway is a tiny program that reads the machine and sends only the numbers — part count, running or stopped, tool number, alarms. Nothing else, and nothing can be sent back to the machine.
1
Check you have what you need
Three things, before you start
▼

1. A PC that stays switched on in the factory. Any ordinary Windows PC or mini-PC will do. It must be plugged into the same network as your CNC machines, and it must have internet access. It will run quietly in the background.

2. The IP address of each machine. This looks like 192.168.1.101. Your machine supplier or maintenance engineer will know it. If nobody knows it yet, that is fine — do Step 7 with the test machine first and come back to this later.

3. Permission to add a setting to your website hosting. That is Step 3. If somebody else manages your Vercel account, send them Step 3 only.

Why a separate PC? A CNC controller is not built to face the internet and must never be exposed to it. The gateway PC is the safe go-between: it can see the machines, and only it talks outward.
2
Create your secret key
A password that lets your factory PC send data in — and keeps everyone else out
▼
Press the button. It makes a long random key on this computer. You will paste the same key in two places: on your hosting (Step 3) and in the factory PC's settings file (Step 6). They must match exactly.
Keep this key private. Anyone who has it can send machine readings into your system. If it ever leaks, generate a new one and redo Steps 3 and 6. It is shown here once and is not saved anywhere — copy it somewhere safe now.
3
Put the key on your hosting
Done once, in your Vercel account, in a web browser
▼

1. Open vercel.com and sign in.

2. Click your IDMS project.

3. Go to Settings, then Environment Variables.

4. Add a new one. Type the name exactly as below — capital letters and underscores matter:

CNC_GATEWAY_KEY

5. In the Value box, paste the key from Step 2.

6. Tick all three environments (Production, Preview, Development) and press Save.

7. Go to the Deployments tab and press Redeploy on the newest one. This last step is the one people forget — the key does not take effect until the site is redeployed.

Until this is done, the factory PC will be turned away with the message “Invalid machine gateway key”. That message means Step 3 was missed or the key does not match.
4
Install the gateway on the factory PC
Two downloads and one folder copy
▼

On the factory PC (not this one):

1. Open nodejs.org and download the version marked LTS. Install it, pressing Next through every screen. Nothing needs changing.

2. Copy the machine-gateway folder from your IDMS files onto that PC. Put it somewhere easy to find, such as C:\ironvale-gateway.

3. That is all for now. Step 6 creates the settings file that goes inside that folder.

5
Tell it about your machines
Add one line per machine — or start with the test machine to prove it works
▼
Not sure of your machine's details yet? Press Add a test machine below. It pretends to be a CNC and produces realistic readings, so you can finish every step and see the live screen working today. Delete it once a real machine is connected.
Not sure about “How it connects”? Leave it on MTConnect and ask your machine supplier whether an MTConnect agent is switched on, and on which port. Most machines made after roughly 2015 support it. Port 5000 is the usual answer.
6
Create the settings file
Written for you — copy it, or download it ready to use
▼
This is built from your machines in Step 5 and your key from Step 2. Save it as config.json inside the machine-gateway folder on the factory PC.
Add a machine in Step 5 first.
The file contains your secret key. Do not email it and do not put it in a shared drive that other companies can read.
7
Start it, and check the data arrives
The moment of truth
▼

1. On the factory PC, open the machine-gateway folder.

2. Double-click start-gateway.cmd.

3. A black window opens. If it says Gateway running: 1 machine(s) and then stays quiet, it is working. Leave the window open — closing it stops the readings.

Any red text in that window is telling you what is wrong. Match it against the table further down.

4. Now press the button below. It asks the IDMS whether anything has arrived.

If something is not working

Find the message you can see, and do what the right column says. These cover nearly everything that goes wrong.
What you seeWhat it means and what to do
“No CNC machines connected yet” on the Live Monitor Nothing has arrived. The gateway is not running, or it cannot reach the internet, or Step 3 was not finished with a redeploy. Look at the black window on the factory PC.
IDMS ingest 401 in the black window The keys do not match. The key in config.json must be character-for-character the same as CNC_GATEWAY_KEY on Vercel — and the site must have been redeployed after adding it.
IDMS ingest 404 The address is wrong. In config.json, idmsIngestUrl must end with /api/cnc — nothing after it.
IDMS unreachable The factory PC has no internet, or a firewall is blocking it. Open your IDMS site in a browser on that same PC. If it does not open, it is a network problem, not a settings problem.
MTConnect HTTP 404, or the machine shows OFFLINE The gateway reached the machine's address but found nothing there. The IP or port is wrong, or the MTConnect agent is not switched on. Ask your machine supplier to confirm both.
Unsupported adapter “How it connects” was set to something that is not installed. Use MTConnect, the JSON/HTTP option, or the test machine.
The test machine works, a real one does not This is good news: your key, your address and your internet are all correct. The problem is only between the gateway PC and that machine — an IP, a port, or the agent not being switched on.
Part count does not match the machine's own counter Do not put this into production yet. Run one machine for a full shift and compare against the machine's own counter before trusting the figures or connecting more.
Not built yet
Drag the balloon to where the number reads clearly; drag the small ring at the other end of the leader onto the exact feature it points at. The line follows, at any angle. Use the list on the left to add a characteristic the AI missed, correct one it read wrongly, or delete one that is not on the drawing. Everything you change here is saved against the enquiry — the balloon drawing, the drawing-data table, the quotation and every screen the part reaches afterwards all read it, and the printed sheet then keeps your positions exactly rather than laying them out itself.
Ask the assistant
